1.explanation:
• src/ol/proj/proj4.js  
  This module picks up the proj4.defs[code].axis string and passes it straight into OL’s Projection constructor as axisOrientation.  After proj4js 2.6.1 changed its axis codes to follow EPSG metadata, OL’s simple pass-through no longer matches OL’s expectations and breaks the downstream logic.  

• src/ol/proj/transforms.js  
  OL’s proj4 integration registers forward/inverse functions under keys like “EPSG:2180→EPSG:3857”.  If the axisOrientation in the Projection instances is wrong, those transforms get called with the wrong [x,y] ordering.  Fixing registration or invocation here is part of correcting the reprojection.  

• src/ol/tilegrid/WMTS.js  
  To set the WMTS TileGrid origins, OL inspects projection.getAxisOrientation(), and when substr(0,2)=="ne" it swaps the TopLeftCorner coords.  Because axisOrientation is now coming from the new proj4js value, OL erroneously toggles (or doesn’t toggle) the swap, giving the tile grid a wrong origin and causing imagery to appear rotated.  

• src/ol/reproj/Triangulation.js  
  The reprojection triangulation builds meshes by repeatedly transforming corner coordinates via getTransform(proj1,proj2).  The wrong axis order in the registered transforms feeds directly into this algorithm, skewing the entire reprojection mesh.  Correcting the axisOrientation at registration or normalizing inputs in Triangulation fixes the rotations.
1.bug_scenario:
When upgrading proj4js from 2.6.0 to 2.6.1 in an OpenLayers 6.3.2‐dev build, all externally served WMTS (EPSG:2180) or OSM (EPSG:3857) layers get a consistent “rotation” when reprojected into a view with a different projection.  
– With proj4js 2.6.0 both Mercator (EPSG:3857) and WMTS (EPSG:2180) layers draw perfectly under both views.  
– After the proj4js 2.6.1 axis‐order change, viewing a Mercator view with an EPSG:2180 WMTS source produces a rotated ortho image, and vice versa.  
This clearly points to a mismatch in how OL registers and uses the new proj4js axis‐orientation definitions and applies them both in the projection registry and in the WMTS tile grid origin logic, causing the reprojection pipeline to mis‐order axes and skew the imagery.
